content:
backlog doctor: integrity check command for graph consistency

Backlog's graph store has 249+ items with complex relationships: dependency edges, supersession chains, audit-log event nodes, plan attachments, claim states. There is no command to verify structural integrity.

Possible corruption modes that are currently invisible:
- Dependency target humanId that doesn't exist (orphan edge)
- Superseded item that still has live claims against it
- Audit-log event pointing to a stale or deleted nodeId
- Claim on an item that's in a terminal status (FIXED, RESOLVED) — should have been released
- Item with status OPEN but zero citations or body (zombie entry)
- Plan referenced by items but the plan node doesn't exist

Desired: backlog doctor command that runs a battery of integrity checks and reports:
- PASS/FAIL per check
- For failures: the item humanId and the specific violation
- Optionally: --fix to auto-resolve simple issues (release stale claims, remove orphan dependencies)
- Exit code 0 if all pass, non-zero if any fail (for CI gating)

Checks should be defined as simple query-based rules so new ones can be added without changing the doctor command itself.

dispatch-cli has no bin entry in package.json so npx @adhd/dispatch-cli does not work

dispatch-cli is an entrypoint package (entrypoint/dispatch-cli/) but its package.json has no bin field. Unlike backlog (bin: backlog) and apigen-cli (bin: apigen), dispatch-cli cannot be invoked as npx @adhd/dispatch-cli --help or dispatch --help after install.

Impact: The CLI is unfindable and unusable as a CLI tool. The existing --help bug (BUG-DISPATCH-001: --help doesn't work either) compounds this — even if bin were added, --help wouldn't display commands.

Fix: Add a bin entry to entrypoint/dispatch-cli/package.json pointing at a shebanged entry script. Requires resolving BUG-DISPATCH-001 first (--help handling) or at least alongside it.

content:
published-state.json needs a prune command for stale entries

published-state.json tracks 54 packages with version and integrity data. If a package is unpublished from npm, renamed, or deprecated, its entry stays in the cache forever. There is no mechanism to remove stale entries.

Over time this will accumulate cruft: packages that were renamed still referenced under old names, retired packages still in the list, version bumps that are no longer relevant because the package was superseded.

Desired: A reconcile --prune mode (or separate command) that:
1. Lists all entries in published-state.json
2. Checks each against the actual workspace projects (the project.json or package.json in the repo)
3. Removes entries for packages that no longer exist in the workspace
4. Reports removed entries to stdout for audit
5. Has a --dry-run mode that shows what would be removed without writing

Also: if a package is republished under a different name, the old name entry should be prunable.

meta_parsed.title: published-state.json needs a prune command for stale entries
meta_parsed.body:
published-state.json tracks 54 packages with version and integrity data. If a package is unpublished from npm, renamed, or deprecated, its entry stays in the cache forever. There is no mechanism to remove stale entries.

Over time this will accumulate cruft: packages that were renamed still referenced under old names, retired packages still in the list, version bumps that are no longer relevant because the package was superseded.

Desired: A reconcile --prune mode (or separate command) that:
1. Lists all entries in published-state.json
2. Checks each against the actual workspace projects (the project.json or package.json in the repo)
3. Removes entries for packages that no longer exist in the workspace
4. Reports removed entries to stdout for audit
5. Has a --dry-run mode that shows what would be removed without writing

Also: if a package is republished under a different name, the old name entry should be prunable.

Teach doc-cartographer how to use GitNexus tools for code intelligence during capability discovery

The doc-cartographer agent type has gitnexus_query, gitnexus_context, and gitnexus_impact tools available, but its system prompt does not instruct it to use them. During the dispatch-cli cataloging, the cartographer was told to 'drive GitNexus' and immediately started using gitnexus_query to find execution flows, gitnexus_context to understand symbol relationships, and gitnexus_impact to determine blast radius. This produced better capability descriptions than the prior text-only grep-based approach.

**Problem**: The cartographer's default behavior is grep + file listing. It doesn't naturally reach for GitNexus unless explicitly told to. The dispatch-cli run succeeded because the prompt happened to include that instruction.

**Fix**: Add to the doc-cartographer's system prompt or instructions:
- Always start capability discovery with gitnexus_query for the package name to find its execution flows
- Use gitnexus_context for each major export symbol to understand callers, callees, and relationships
- Use gitnexus_impact to assess risk tier before any recommended changes
- When gitnexus warns the index is stale, run npx gitnexus analyze first

This would produce richer capability descriptions (call graph depth, consumer relationships, execution flow counts) without needing the dispatcher to remember to request it every time.

content:
Cartographer should catalog each project's exposed interfaces in a dedicated file

The doc-cartographer currently catalogs capabilities at the package level — what a package does, its key exports, its verification commands. But it does not produce a structured interface catalog: the full list of public exports, their TypeScript signatures, their parameter types, and their return types.

This gap became visible during the dispatch-cli audit: the cartographer correctly identified 12 capabilities, but to understand the actual API surface of api.ts (7 async functions with specific parameter types), I had to read the source file directly. The catalog told me WHAT existed but not the exact shape of each export.

**Desired**: The cartographer should produce a structured `interfaces.json` (or `exports.md`) per scope that catalogs:
- Every public export from the package's entry point (index.ts or the configured main/module/exports field)
- For each export: name, kind (function/class/type/const), full TypeScript signature, JSDoc summary, parameter list with types, return type
- For packages with multiple entry points (api.ts + index.ts + bin/cli.ts), catalog each separately
- The interface file should be machine-readable (JSON) AND human-readable (Markdown)
- Generated via ts-morph program analysis, not by hand

**Relationship**:
- FEAT-DOC-STEWARD-001 (programmatic coverage report) would use this to determine which exports have matching documentation
- FEAT-DOC-STEWARD-006 (teach cartographer GitNexus) provides the call-graph depth this interface catalog would complement
- The dispatch-cli demonstrates the need: api.ts has 7 async function exports, index.ts re-exports them + core.ts internals, bin/cli.ts registers Commander commands — three different interface surfaces that a consumer needs to navigate

content:
Reconcile three independent dispatcher concepts: dispatch-cli, backlog, and agent-mcp

The @adhd ecosystem has three separate dispatcher implementations with overlapping concerns but zero shared architecture:

**1. dispatch-cli / dispatch-* packages** (entrypoint/dispatch-cli/ + packages/dispatch/)
- Purpose: DAG task orchestration — validate, snapshot, optimize, run, calibrate
- Abstraction: DagClient (CRUD over dag.json), DagSnapshot (cost estimation), DispatchUnit (packed work), OrchestratorCycle (snapshot→optimize→dispatch→persist)
- Runner: MockAgentRunner (default, free) or AgentMcpRunner (paid, spawns agent-mcp)
- Status: Shipped, 12 capabilities, 30 tests pass, 0.0.4 on npm

**2. backlog** (entrypoint/backlog/)
- Purpose: Graph-based multi-agent backlog management — CRUD, lifecycle, claims, dependencies
- Abstraction: GraphBacklogStore (SQLite+SOX nodes/edges), client.ts (34 ops), audit-log events
- Dispatch pattern: Item lifecycle transitions (start-work, transition-status, claim/renew/release), dependency graph traversal
- Status: Shipped, phase-3 migration active, MCP+CLI+HTTP transports

**3. agent-mcp** (entrypoint/agent-mcp/)
- Purpose: AI agent runtime — spawn, delegate, coordinate agents across providers
- Abstraction: Orchestrator (task dispatch loop), ProviderRouter, SessionStore, ToolRegistry
- Dispatch pattern: Provider-agnostic task dispatch with hooks (budget, sanitize, usage accounting), SSE streaming, HITL
- Status: Shipped, 12 packages published, claudecli provider has 3.4x perf advantage

**Why reconcile is needed**:
- dispatch-cli's AgentMcpRunner spawns agent-mcp as a subprocess — agent-mcp doesn't know it's being used by dispatch-cli
- backlog's claim/release pattern is a form of task dispatch but incompatible with dispatch-cli's DagClient model
- All three have their own concept of 'dispatch' but no shared interface, type, or protocol
- A cross-repo backlog item (FEAT-BACKLOG-002) would need to interact with dispatch-cli's DAG model
- Enrichment plugins (FEAT-BACKLOG-001, dispatch-plugin-*) would benefit from a shared event/hook model

**Not proposing a merge** — the three serve different purposes. But the boundaries, overlaps, and integration points should be explicitly documented so a future developer knows which dispatcher to extend and how they relate. A reconciliation document should cover:
- What each dispatcher does
- Where they overlap
- Where they are intentionally different
- How they interact today (dispatch-cli -> spawns agent-mcp)
- How they could interact in the future (backlog items driving dispatch-cli DAGs?)
- Which abstraction would be shared vs which are intentionally separate

agent-mcp claudecli triage fleet: default 60s provider timeout + gitnexus MCP singleton contention caused ~72% first-pass failure under 29-way concurrency

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, dispatching 29 concurrent one-shot Haiku triage tasks via `mcp__agent-mcp__task` (agent `agentmcp-triage-haiku`, provider `type:claudecli`, `model:claude-haiku-4-5`, with `mcpServers.gitnexus` wired to `/Users/nix/.local/bin/gitnexus-singleton.sh`) to triage 29 agent-mcp-related backlog items.

**Symptom 1 — mass timeout:** Of the first 29 dispatched tasks, 21 (~72%) failed with `error: "Provider call timed out after 60000ms. Increase timeoutMs on the agent's provider config."` Only 2 completed on the first pass. The claudecli provider's default `timeoutMs` is 60000ms with no override set on the agent definition.

**Symptom 2 — gitnexus MCP singleton disconnects under load:** During the same window, the orchestrating session's own `mcp__gitnexus__*` tools were reported disconnected ("MCP server disconnected") and later reconnected twice, correlating with the burst of concurrent `claude` CLI subprocesses each also connecting to the same `gitnexus-singleton.sh` stdio server. `gitnexus-singleton.sh` (`~/.local/bin/`) is presumably a single-instance wrapper; its behavior under N-way concurrent client connections (queuing vs. contention vs. crash-restart) is unverified.

**Root cause (partial):** (a) 60000ms is too short for a real per-task workload that does Read/Grep/Bash plus at least one gitnexus MCP round-trip, especially once N candidate tasks queue for a limited concurrency pool — the timeout clock appears to start at task creation, so queued-but-not-yet-running tasks can burn most of their budget waiting for a slot. (b) the shared gitnexus singleton is a likely contention point / possible restart-under-load, which would explain both the timeouts (slow tool responses) and the orchestrator-visible MCP disconnects.

**Verified fix applied this session (partial mitigation, not a root-cause fix):** `mcp__agent-mcp__agent_update` on `agentmcp-triage-haiku` to set `provider.timeoutMs: 300000`. Retried tasks after this change ran past the 60s mark without failing (confirmed via `mcp__agent-mcp__task_list` timestamps), and several completed successfully with full GitNexus-informed verdicts.

**Fix direction:**
1. Raise agent-mcp's claudecli provider default `timeoutMs` (or at minimum document that any real (non-trivial) one-shot agent needs an explicit override — the 60s default is a footgun for the common case).
2. Determine whether the timeout clock should start at dequeue (call start) rather than task creation, so queued tasks aren't penalized for someone else's concurrency.
3. Investigate `gitnexus-singleton.sh`'s behavior under N concurrent stdio client connections — does it multiplex, queue, or crash/restart? If it crash-restarts under load, that would explain the orchestrator's own tool disconnect/reconnect during the same window.
4. Consider a lower default fan-out / concurrency cap recommendation for agent-mcp task dispatch when many sessions all declare the same MCP server, until (3) is resolved.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: mcp__agent-mcp__task_list failed-status entries showing `error: "Provider call timed out after 60000ms..."` across 21 of 29 first-pass tasks; 2: system-reminders in this session reporting mcp__gitnexus__* tools disconnected then reconnected twice during the same dispatch window; 3: mcp__agent-mcp__agent_update raising agentmcp-triage-haiku's provider.timeoutMs to 300000, after which retried tasks ran past 60s without failing]

content:
agent-mcp needs a native bulk/parallel task-dispatch primitive (agent()+task() fan-out is manual, error-prone, and encourages unsafe concurrency)

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, dispatching 31 independent one-shot Haiku triage tasks against backlog items via `mcp__agent-mcp__*` (see BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001 for the incident this surfaced).

**Problem:** There is no way to fan out N independent tasks in one call. To triage 31 items I had to, by hand: call `agent({name})` N times to get N session_ids, then `task({session_id, prompt, background:true})` N times, while manually building and maintaining a session_id↔task_id↔humanId mapping in scratch files across the conversation. This is exactly the kind of bookkeeping a tool should own:
- Every fan-out is an opportunity for a transcription error (I made one myself early in this session, dispatching a placeholder args array to a *different* tool because I'd lost track of which payload belonged to which call).
- There's no way to express "run these N independent prompts, cap concurrency at K" — the caller has to either fire all N at once (which caused the 72% failure rate in BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001, likely from gitnexus-singleton contention) or hand-roll serialization via `depends_on` chains (which works, verified in this session, but requires manually threading N-1 dependency edges through N sequential tool calls — itself an N-step bookkeeping task).

**Fix direction:** Add a batch/fan-out entrypoint, e.g. `tasks_batch({agent_name | session_ids, prompts: string[], concurrency?: number})` that:
1. Creates sessions internally (or reuses supplied ones) and dispatches all prompts, honoring an optional `concurrency` cap so the caller doesn't have to choose between "all at once" and "fully serial via depends_on chaining."
2. Returns an array of `{index, task_id}` (or `{index, result}` if run synchronously to completion) so the caller never has to hand-maintain the mapping.
3. Composes with the existing `depends_on`/`on_upstream_failure` fields for cases that need real ordering, but doesn't require the caller to hand-build a chain for the common "N independent items, throttled" case.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: this session's manual session_id/task_id/humanId mapping tracked in scratch JSON files across ~15 tool-call rounds to triage 31 backlog items; 2: BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001 — the same session's incident report showing all-at-once fan-out causing 72% first-pass failure, and a subsequent depends_on-chained serialization (manually built, one tool call per link) resolving it with zero repeat failures]

content:
gitnexus-singleton.sh needs a documented, verified concurrency contract for N simultaneous stdio MCP clients across the workspace

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, during a 29-way concurrent agent-mcp task dispatch (see BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001) where each dispatched Haiku triage agent's `mcpServers.gitnexus` config pointed at the same `/Users/nix/.local/bin/gitnexus-singleton.sh`, while the orchestrating Claude Code session *also* had its own live `mcp__gitnexus__*` connection to (presumably) the same singleton.

**Symptom:** During the burst of ~29 concurrent `claude` CLI subprocesses each connecting to `gitnexus-singleton.sh`, the orchestrating session's own `mcp__gitnexus__*` tools were reported disconnected ("MCP server disconnected") and reconnected twice within a few minutes — with no action taken by the orchestrator that would explain a disconnect. This correlates suspiciously with the concurrent client burst, but was not root-caused in this session (no direct log access to gitnexus-singleton.sh's internals).

**Open questions this item exists to answer:**
1. Does `gitnexus-singleton.sh` genuinely enforce single-instance (one shared process, multiplexing N stdio client connections), or does each client connection risk killing/restarting the singleton (which would explain the orchestrator's observed disconnects)?
2. What is the supported/tested concurrent-client count? Is there a documented limit, or was this simply never exercised at this concurrency before?
3. If it's a genuine bottleneck (not just a query queue), does every `claude` CLI subprocess spawned by agent-mcp with `mcpServers.gitnexus` configured need its own gitnexus instance instead of sharing the singleton — and if so, what's the resource cost of N parallel GitNexus indexes/processes for a large repo (adhd itself is 29k+ symbols / 43k+ relationships)?
4. Should agent-mcp-dispatched agents avoid wiring `mcpServers.gitnexus` to the same singleton path the interactive session uses, to avoid cross-contaminating the interactive user's own GitNexus session?

**Fix direction:** Instrument or read `gitnexus-singleton.sh` (and whatever process it wraps) to determine actual behavior under concurrent connections; document the supported concurrency model; if it doesn't safely support N-way concurrent clients, either (a) make it multiplex/queue safely, or (b) provide a documented pattern for dispatched agents to use an isolated/ephemeral GitNexus instance instead of the shared singleton.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: system-reminders in this session reporting mcp__gitnexus__* tools disconnected then reconnected twice, timed to overlap with a burst of ~29 concurrent claude CLI subprocess dispatches each configured with mcpServers.gitnexus pointing at /Users/nix/.local/bin/gitnexus-singleton.sh; 2: BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001 — originating incident, correlating the same window's mass task timeouts with this contention]

content:
agent_update silently does not affect open sessions - no signal on the resulting task failure points operators back to the real cause

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, while fixing BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001 by raising `agentmcp-triage-haiku`'s `provider.timeoutMs` via `agent_update`.

**Problem:** `agent_update` bumps the stored agent definition's version and `agent_read` correctly reflects the new config, but sessions created before the update keep running on their original snapshot (this is documented behavior per `guide()`: "The agent snapshot is taken at session creation, so updating the definition later does not affect open sessions"). However, nothing in the `task` tool's response or error surfaces this: retrying a timed-out task on its original `session_id` after `agent_update` produces the *exact same* `"Provider call timed out after 60000ms"` error, with no indication that the fix I just applied didn't actually apply to this session. I burned two retry rounds (5 of 14, then had to diagnose it by comparing `agent_read`'s reported timeoutMs against the repeat failures) before realizing I needed brand-new sessions.

**Fix direction:** Either (a) have `task`'s error/response include the session's effective config version alongside the failure, so a mismatch against the current stored definition is visible without cross-referencing `agent_read` by hand; or (b) surface a warning in `agent_update`'s response listing any currently-open sessions on that agent that will NOT receive the update, so operators know upfront which sessions need replacing rather than discovering it via a repeat failure.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: mcp__agent-mcp__task_list — 5 of 14 retries dispatched via task() on pre-existing session_ids failed again with the identical 60000ms timeout error after agent_update had already raised provider.timeoutMs to 300000 on the stored definition; 2: guide() text confirming session-snapshot-at-creation is intended behavior, but not surfaced anywhere in the task-failure path]

guide() omits the task tool's depends_on/on_upstream_failure DAG-chaining capability, which is the natural fix for shared-resource contention under fan-out

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, while recovering from BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001 (mass timeout under 29-way concurrent task dispatch, likely from gitnexus-singleton contention).

**Problem:** The `task` tool's schema exposes `depends_on` (array of upstream task_ids) and `on_upstream_failure` ('fail'|'skip'), which let a caller serialize a batch of otherwise-independent tasks into a dependency chain — exactly the mechanism needed to avoid overwhelming a shared, contention-sensitive resource (like the gitnexus singleton in this incident). This worked perfectly when applied (zero repeat failures across two chained batches of 9 and 7 items, versus a 72%/36% failure rate when dispatched in parallel). But `mcp__agent-mcp__guide()` — which explicitly documents Workflows 0-4 (one-shot, basic, background+polling, delegation, multi-turn) — never mentions `depends_on`/`on_upstream_failure` at all. I only used it because a human operator suggested it mid-session; nothing in the tool's own documentation would have led me there.

**Fix direction:** Add a "Workflow 5 — serialized chain via depends_on" section to `guide()`'s output, explicitly calling out that this is the recommended pattern when many tasks share a contention-sensitive external resource (a shared MCP server, a rate-limited API, etc.), as an alternative to firing everything in parallel.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: mcp__agent-mcp__guide() full output captured this session — Workflows 0-4 documented, no mention of depends_on/on_upstream_failure despite both being present in the task tool's own JSONSchema; 2: two depends_on-chained dispatches of 9 and 7 backlog-triage items respectively, both completing with zero repeat timeouts, versus 21/29 and 5/14 failures on the equivalent parallel/retried-on-stale-session dispatches earlier in the same session]

content:
task_list has no session_id/agent-name/humanId filter, forcing full-instance scans to check a single batch's progress

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, polling the status of a 31-item backlog-triage batch dispatched via `mcp__agent-mcp__task`.

**Problem:** `task_list`'s only filter parameters are `status`, `is_ephemeral`, and `session_id` (single value). There is no way to ask "show me the tasks belonging to agent X" or "show me tasks for this list of session_ids" or filter/search by content. Checking progress on my 31-item batch meant pulling every task in the entire agent-mcp instance matching a given status — including unrelated tasks from hours-earlier, completely separate work (an 8-file A/B performance test, diagnostic probes, etc.) that happened to share the same status at poll time. I had to cross-reference the returned blob against a hand-maintained task_id→humanId map in scratch files just to know which results were mine.

**Fix direction:** Add optional `session_ids: string[]` (plural) and/or `agent_name: string` filters to `task_list`, so a caller tracking one batch/agent doesn't have to filter a global result set client-side.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: mcp__agent-mcp__task_list calls this session returning entries from unrelated prior work (an 8-file A/B edit-verify test, diagnostic probe tasks) mixed in with the 31-item triage batch being tracked, requiring client-side cross-referencing against a hand-built task_id-to-humanId map]

content:
task_list/result return full unbounded prompt+result text for every matching task, with no field projection - routinely exceeds tool-output token limits

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, polling a 31-item backlog-triage batch.

**Problem:** `task_list` returns the full `prompt` and `result` text for every task matching the status filter — not just the current batch, every historical task in the agent-mcp instance at that status. Several polls in this session returned 55-76KB payloads and were truncated by the harness's tool-output token limit, forcing a fallback to reading the saved raw-output file via `Read`/`Bash`+`jq` instead of consuming the tool result directly. This happened repeatedly (at least 4 times) across a single triage run, each time costing an extra round-trip just to extract 2-3 fields (`id`, `status`, `error`/short result summary) from a payload where the caller only needed the failure/completion state.

**Fix direction:** Add a `fields: string[]` (or `summary: boolean`) projection parameter to `task_list` (and optionally `result`) so a caller doing bulk status polling can request e.g. `["id","status","error"]` and get a compact response, reserving the full prompt+result payload for when a specific task_id is actually being inspected.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: at least 4 mcp__agent-mcp__task_list calls in this session exceeded the tool-output token limit (55.9KB, 61.9KB, 67.2KB, 75.7KB observed) and were redirected to saved files, requiring a separate Bash+jq/python parse step each time solely to extract id/status/error fields already present but drowned in unbounded prompt/result text]

content:
ephemeral (agent_name-mode) task context can be lost on server restart with no recovery path other than silent re-creation

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, observed on an unrelated prior ephemeral task in this same agent-mcp instance while polling `task_list` during this session's backlog-triage work (not something I triggered directly this session, but directly observed in the live instance's task history).

**Symptom:** `task_list` shows a historical ephemeral (`agent_name`-mode, `isEphemeral:true`) task with `status:"failed"` and `error: "Ephemeral task context lost on server restart; create a new task."` The task had originally been dispatched hours earlier (`createdAt` well before the failure's `updatedAt`), meaning it sat in a state where a server restart silently invalidated its in-memory-only context, and the failure was only surfaced the next time something polled it — not proactively.

**Impact:** Per `guide()`, ephemeral mode is documented as "nothing is written to the DB beyond the agent read" — by design, ephemeral tasks trade durability for statelessness. But a caller has no way to know a server restart happened between dispatch and poll, and no automatic retry/notification path; the task simply sits until someone happens to check it, then fails with a message whose only remedy is "create a new task" (i.e., silently re-run from scratch, potentially duplicating work already believed in-flight).

**Fix direction:** Either (a) make ephemeral tasks fail fast at restart time (proactively mark all in-flight ephemeral tasks as failed at server startup, rather than lazily on next poll) so callers see the failure promptly instead of an indefinite `pending`/`running` state that silently expired; or (b) if feasible, persist just enough of an ephemeral task's initial request (not full context) to auto-resubmit it transparently after a restart, since the whole point of `agent_name` mode is that it has no meaningful context to lose beyond the original prompt.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: mcp__agent-mcp__task_list(status:'failed') entry task id 7e12ff0e-a623-4984-8912-241ff15d76d5, isEphemeral:true, createdAt 2026-07-25T01:24:30.727Z, error 'Ephemeral task context lost on server restart; create a new task.', updatedAt 2026-07-25T01:55:48.092Z (~31 min gap between dispatch and the failure being recorded, only surfaced via this session's later poll)]

Recommend filing a new, correctly-scoped bug titled something like 'orphaned-task recovery sweep never queries status=running, tasks crash-stuck forever' against entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/index.ts:362-377 and packages/agent/agent-engine-orchestrator/src/tools/task.ts, and routing it to architect/devops for a fix design (widen the startup query to include 'running' and 'awaiting_input', and decide fail-vs-resume semantics for each).

Closed after an independent corroboration pass over the 49 DEAD-verdict candidates produced by run wf_28c6a91a-4c9. That run is known unreliable (82% of its triage agents had no graph access), so every verdict was re-tested against the item's REAL current content rather than trusted. no dry-run/handshake verification for an agent definition's mcpServers config before a real task burns its timeout discovering a misconfiguration

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, wiring `mcpServers.gitnexus` (stdio, command `/Users/nix/.local/bin/gitnexus-singleton.sh`) into a new agent definition (`agentmcp-triage-haiku`) via `agent_create`.

**Problem:** There is no way to confirm an agent's `mcpServers` configuration actually connects and exposes the expected tools before dispatching a real task against it. The only feedback loop is: create the agent, open a session, dispatch a task, wait (up to the provider timeout) for either a tool-using result or a failure — by which point a bad `command`, wrong `args`, or a server that doesn't expose the tools the system prompt references has already cost a full timeout window. In this session that risk was masked by the concurrency incident (BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001) making it hard to tell "gitnexus config is wrong" apart from "gitnexus is contended/slow," and was only resolved by seeing a real triage task cite actual GitNexus tool output.

**Fix direction:** Add a lightweight `agent_verify_mcp({name})` (or fold into `agent_create`/`agent_update` as an optional `verify: true` flag) that spins up each configured MCP server, performs the handshake, and returns the reachable tool list (or a clear per-server connection error) — without invoking the model or spending any of the task-provider timeout budget.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: agent_create call this session wiring mcpServers.gitnexus with no verification step available before the first real task dispatch; 2: BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001 — same session, where task timeouts made it genuinely ambiguous for several retry rounds whether the failure was a bad MCP config or contention, a distinction a handshake-only verify call would have resolved immediately]

content:
Architect generic bulk/parallel operation support into apigen's extract/plugin pipeline (not per-consumer, not per-transport)

**Context:** Filed as a follow-up to a 2026-07-25 session that hit the same gap twice from two different angles:
1. **DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001** — agent-mcp needs a native way to fan out N independent tasks (discovered while manually dispatching 31 backlog-triage tasks, one `agent()`+`task()` call pair at a time, with hand-maintained bookkeeping).
2. **FEAT-BACKLOG-005** (pre-existing, filed earlier) — "Bulk and batch operations for CLI and MCP transports" for the `backlog` package specifically.

Both are consumer-level asks for the same missing capability. **This item is the architectural one level up:** apigen (`@adhd/apigen-*`) is the shared extract/composeSchemas/plugin.run pipeline that both `backlog` and (per **FEAT-AGENT-001**'s proposed refactor) `agent-mcp` are built on, projecting one TypeScript client to CLI/MCP/HTTP from a single source of truth. If bulk/parallel operation support is built once, generically, into apigen's pipeline — rather than bolted onto each consumer's hand-written client — every apigen-driven entrypoint (backlog, a refactored agent-mcp, and any future one) gets it for free, and FEAT-BACKLOG-005 + DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001 become consequences of this rather than separate implementations that will drift.

**Why this needs architecting, not just coding (per repo convention):**
- **Client-shape design:** does a bulk operation appear as a new first-class client method (`bulkCreateItems(items[])`), a wrapper/decorator apigen auto-generates for any existing single-item operation (`operationName + 'Bulk'`), or a generic `batch(ops[])` envelope that fans out arbitrary calls? Each has different implications for CLI ergonomics (`backlog bulk-create --file items.json` vs `backlog create --batch`), MCP tool proliferation, and HTTP route design (`POST /items/bulk` vs repeated `POST /items`).
- **Concurrency model:** apigen's generated MCP/CLI/HTTP surfaces need a consistent answer for concurrency caps, partial-failure semantics (all-or-nothing vs per-item result with some failed), and ordering guarantees (independent fan-out vs the `depends_on`-style DAG chaining that proved necessary for agent-mcp under gitnexus-singleton contention — see **BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001** / **DEBT-GITNEXUS-CONCURRENCY-001**). A generic apigen-level solution should let a consumer opt into throttled-parallel, fully-serial, or DAG-chained execution without hand-rolling it per package.
- **Schema/codegen impact:** apigen's `extract`/`composeSchemas` step would need to recognize and mark bulk-capable operations, and each transport plugin (CLI/Commander, MCP/stdio, HTTP/Fastify) needs its own consistent projection of that marker — this is exactly the kind of cross-cutting extraction-pipeline change the repo's plan-state-machine methodology exists for (multi-package, must-not-break-existing-consumers, needs explicit red→green acceptance criteria per transport).

**Fix direction:** Author a plan-state-machine plan (via the `workflow:plan-state-machine` skill, per this repo's convention for cross-cutting architectural changes) covering: (1) design the bulk-operation client-shape convention apigen will recognize, (2) extend `apigen-core-client`'s extract/composeSchemas to detect and annotate bulk-capable operations, (3) extend each transport plugin (`apigen-plugin-cli-output`, the MCP plugin, the HTTP/Fastify plugin) to project bulk operations consistently, (4) migrate `backlog` (closing FEAT-BACKLOG-005) and the proposed apigen-refactored `agent-mcp` (closing DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001) onto the new generic mechanism as proof-of-adoption, with real integration tests per this repo's verification standard (real components, not mocks).

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001 — consumer-level need discovered dispatching 31 backlog-triage tasks by hand via agent()+task(); 2: FEAT-BACKLOG-005 — pre-existing backlog-specific bulk/batch-operations item this generalizes; 3: FEAT-AGENT-001 — proposed agent-mcp-to-apigen refactor that would make agent-mcp a second consumer of this same generic mechanism; 4: BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001/DEBT-GITNEXUS-CONCURRENCY-001 — same session's evidence that a naive all-at-once bulk dispatch can overwhelm a shared contended resource, motivating the concurrency-model design question above]

(2) Corrected an earlier wrong assumption: entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts does NOT use createApiPackage or the v2 --use MountCapability loader — it hand-wires extract()/composeSchemas()/plugin.run() directly (v1 OutputPlugin contract). Next step: architect review of this design, scoped explicitly to apigen-core-client/apigen-engine-runtime + the consumer-authoring experience only (not the pre-existing per-plugin implementation gaps tracked by FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000's children, which are out of scope for this item's review)."},{"by":"architect-reviewer","at":"2026-07-25T18:28:22.770Z","text":"Architect review (2026-07-25), scoped explicitly to apigen-core-client/apigen-engine-runtime + consumer-authoring experience only (current per-plugin implementation gaps under FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000 were explicitly out of scope for this review).

VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES. Core insight (batch-shaped ops vs. generic fan-out are different problems) is correct; orchestrating fan-out as pure composition over the existing invoke()/Layer stack is sound. Several parts are under-specified in ways that will force breaking changes as new hosts/transports/consumers arrive.

F1 — _batch's single static Operation cannot represent a polymorphic fan-out target. Operation.kind/safe are per-op static classifications transports read to make wire decisions (safe drives HTTP verb/cacheability, kind distinguishes action/query), but _batch's actual behavior varies per-request based on the runtime `operation` string selected in call.data - no static Operation object can carry that. Required change: mount one synthetic op PER DISTINCT KIND present in the batchable set (_batch/query, _batch/action), each with truthful static kind/safe and an operation enum restricted to ids of that kind - keeps the common single-kind case (e.g. agent-mcp's task) at exactly one extra tool/route/command.

F2 — The proposal's example code calls syntheticOp(id, descriptor) which does not exist anywhere as real, exported code - it appears exactly once, in a JSDoc example comment on MountCapability (apigen-core-client/src/lib/plugin.ts:452), never exported. The one real shipped MountCapability (apigen-plugin-health) hand-builds the full ~10-field Operation literal itself, including a locally-reimplemented seg() helper to avoid a cross-package dependency. Required change: extract and ship a REAL syntheticOp(id, descriptor, fields) helper in apigen-core-client as part of this work, and retrofit apigen-plugin-health onto it in the same change so there is exactly one implementation, not two independently-maintained ones.

F3 — No cross-host contract; invokeBatch/MountCapability is TS-only today with nothing to port. PluginLanguage already includes py/rust/go/java, and a Python runtime already exists (packages/apigen/python/apigen_python/runtime.py, its own invoke/invoke_sync) entirely separate from the TS createInvoker/Layer/MountCapability types. MountedOperation.handler's signature is a TS closure type, not expressible in the Python runtime's model at all. Required change: specify BatchOptions/BatchItemResult as a wire-level JSON-Schema IR independent of the TS invokeBatch function signature (the same separation apigen already uses for Operation's type IR generally) so each host runtime implements fan-out against that wire contract, none depending on the TS implementation.

F4 — BatchOptions is missing per-item cancellation/timeout, will force a breaking change. Call.signal is whole-request cancellation already wired per single op; invokeBatch fans out N invoke() calls but never states whether an individual item's failure/timeout can be cancelled independently of the batch, or whether whole-batch abort propagates to in-flight items. Given onItemError:'continue' is the stated default, 'bound one slow item without killing the whole batch' is near-certain to be requested immediately after ship (it's close to the exact motivating scenario - agent-mcp dispatching to a slow external service per call). Required change: state explicitly whether each fanned-out item gets its own signal derived/linked from the batch's signal, and add itemTimeoutMs?: number to BatchOptions now (even as a stub) so the shape doesn't need a breaking revision on first request.

F5 — Two consumption paths (--use loader vs. hand-wired capabilities.mount.operations()) need an explicit equivalence guarantee. Both paths are legitimate but only acceptable if guaranteed to produce IDENTICAL MountedOperation[] output for the same (descriptor, opts) - otherwise a hand-wiring consumer (like backlog) silently forks from CLI behavior as the plugin evolves. Nothing in the current proposal states or tests this. Required change: state it as an explicit invariant and add a conformance test (analogous to apigen-engine-conformance's existing role) that drives both paths against a fixture descriptor and diffs the output.

F6 (non-blocking, just record it) — Tenet 1 compliance (never derive behavior from source annotations) is already satisfied by the exclude opt-out and dynamic per-item validation reuse; worth stating explicitly in the eventual design doc so a future reviewer doesn't re-litigate it.

Reviewer's summary: ship this, but close F1-F4 before the shape hardens into public API. F1 and F3 are the two most consequential for surviving contact with a second host language and a second transport family; F2 and F5 are cheap to fix now and expensive to retrofit later.

meta_parsed.title: Architect generic bulk/parallel operation support into apigen's extract/plugin pipeline (not per-consumer, not per-transport)
meta_parsed.body:
**Context:** Filed as a follow-up to a 2026-07-25 session that hit the same gap twice from two different angles:
1. **DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001** — agent-mcp needs a native way to fan out N independent tasks (discovered while manually dispatching 31 backlog-triage tasks, one `agent()`+`task()` call pair at a time, with hand-maintained bookkeeping).
2. **FEAT-BACKLOG-005** (pre-existing, filed earlier) — "Bulk and batch operations for CLI and MCP transports" for the `backlog` package specifically.

Both are consumer-level asks for the same missing capability. **This item is the architectural one level up:** apigen (`@adhd/apigen-*`) is the shared extract/composeSchemas/plugin.run pipeline that both `backlog` and (per **FEAT-AGENT-001**'s proposed refactor) `agent-mcp` are built on, projecting one TypeScript client to CLI/MCP/HTTP from a single source of truth. If bulk/parallel operation support is built once, generically, into apigen's pipeline — rather than bolted onto each consumer's hand-written client — every apigen-driven entrypoint (backlog, a refactored agent-mcp, and any future one) gets it for free, and FEAT-BACKLOG-005 + DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001 become consequences of this rather than separate implementations that will drift.

**Why this needs architecting, not just coding (per repo convention):**
- **Client-shape design:** does a bulk operation appear as a new first-class client method (`bulkCreateItems(items[])`), a wrapper/decorator apigen auto-generates for any existing single-item operation (`operationName + 'Bulk'`), or a generic `batch(ops[])` envelope that fans out arbitrary calls? Each has different implications for CLI ergonomics (`backlog bulk-create --file items.json` vs `backlog create --batch`), MCP tool proliferation, and HTTP route design (`POST /items/bulk` vs repeated `POST /items`).
- **Concurrency model:** apigen's generated MCP/CLI/HTTP surfaces need a consistent answer for concurrency caps, partial-failure semantics (all-or-nothing vs per-item result with some failed), and ordering guarantees (independent fan-out vs the `depends_on`-style DAG chaining that proved necessary for agent-mcp under gitnexus-singleton contention — see **BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001** / **DEBT-GITNEXUS-CONCURRENCY-001**). A generic apigen-level solution should let a consumer opt into throttled-parallel, fully-serial, or DAG-chained execution without hand-rolling it per package.
- **Schema/codegen impact:** apigen's `extract`/`composeSchemas` step would need to recognize and mark bulk-capable operations, and each transport plugin (CLI/Commander, MCP/stdio, HTTP/Fastify) needs its own consistent projection of that marker — this is exactly the kind of cross-cutting extraction-pipeline change the repo's plan-state-machine methodology exists for (multi-package, must-not-break-existing-consumers, needs explicit red→green acceptance criteria per transport).

**Fix direction:** Author a plan-state-machine plan (via the `workflow:plan-state-machine` skill, per this repo's convention for cross-cutting architectural changes) covering: (1) design the bulk-operation client-shape convention apigen will recognize, (2) extend `apigen-core-client`'s extract/composeSchemas to detect and annotate bulk-capable operations, (3) extend each transport plugin (`apigen-plugin-cli-output`, the MCP plugin, the HTTP/Fastify plugin) to project bulk operations consistently, (4) migrate `backlog` (closing FEAT-BACKLOG-005) and the proposed apigen-refactored `agent-mcp` (closing DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001) onto the new generic mechanism as proof-of-adoption, with real integration tests per this repo's verification standard (real components, not mocks).

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001 — consumer-level need discovered dispatching 31 backlog-triage tasks by hand via agent()+task(); 2: FEAT-BACKLOG-005 — pre-existing backlog-specific bulk/batch-operations item this generalizes; 3: FEAT-AGENT-001 — proposed agent-mcp-to-apigen refactor that would make agent-mcp a second consumer of this same generic mechanism; 4: BUG-AGENTMCP-TRIAGE-CONCURRENCY-001/DEBT-GITNEXUS-CONCURRENCY-001 — same session's evidence that a naive all-at-once bulk dispatch can overwhelm a shared contended resource, motivating the concurrency-model design question above]

notes.text: Design refined through further discussion (2026-07-25), before any architect review: (1) two distinct kinds of 'bulk' identified — author-written batch-shaped operations (e.g. batchCreateItems(items[])) need ZERO apigen changes, they're just ordinary Operations; the real generic gap is N-way fan-out of an EXISTING unmodified single-item operation, which is what DEBT-AGENTMCP-BULK-DISPATCH-001 actually needs. (2) Corrected an earlier wrong assumption: entrypoint/backlog/src/server.ts does NOT use createApiPackage or the v2 --use MountCapability loader — it hand-wires extract()/composeSchemas()/plugin.run() directly (v1 OutputPlugin contract). (3) Confirmed --use IS real, load-bearing machinery elsewhere (apigen serve's health plugin: serve.ts pushes '--use','health' to spawn the CLI pipeline) — so batch should be modeled as a genuine MountCapability plugin loaded via --use, consistent with the openapi/health precedent, while consumers on the hand-wired pattern (backlog-style) invoke the same plugin's capabilities.mount.operations() directly rather than going through the CLI loader. (4) Streaming inclusion (not exclusion) resolved via a two-tier design: Tier 1 (day-1, universal) reuses the EXISTING collectWithPhase/ApiStream machinery (already used by apigen-plugin-mcp's single-op streaming path) to give every batch item - unary or streaming - one uniform terminal BatchItemResult shape, working on all four transports today without requiring any transport to gain new streaming capability. Tier 2 (capability-gated, not deferred) lets transports with true live single-op streaming (HTTP/SSE today) project a live tagged-multiplexed batch stream instead of collecting - see the cross-linked note on FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000 for how that epic's landing automatically upgrades Tier 2 per-transport. Next step: architect review of this design, scoped explicitly to apigen-core-client/apigen-engine-runtime + the consumer-authoring experience only (not the pre-existing per-plugin implementation gaps tracked by FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000's children, which are out of scope for this item's review).

Architect review (2026-07-25), scoped explicitly to apigen-core-client/apigen-engine-runtime + consumer-authoring experience only (current per-plugin implementation gaps under FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-000 were explicitly out of scope for this review).

VERDICT: GO-WITH-CHANGES. Core insight (batch-shaped ops vs. generic fan-out are different problems) is correct; orchestrating fan-out as pure composition over the existing invoke()/Layer stack is sound. Several parts are under-specified in ways that will force breaking changes as new hosts/transports/consumers arrive.

F1 — _batch's single static Operation cannot represent a polymorphic fan-out target. Operation.kind/safe are per-op static classifications transports read to make wire decisions (safe drives HTTP verb/cacheability, kind distinguishes action/query), but _batch's actual behavior varies per-request based on the runtime `operation` string selected in call.data - no static Operation object can carry that. Required change: mount one synthetic op PER DISTINCT KIND present in the batchable set (_batch/query, _batch/action), each with truthful static kind/safe and an operation enum restricted to ids of that kind - keeps the common single-kind case (e.g. agent-mcp's task) at exactly one extra tool/route/command.

F2 — The proposal's example code calls syntheticOp(id, descriptor) which does not exist anywhere as real, exported code - it appears exactly once, in a JSDoc example comment on MountCapability (apigen-core-client/src/lib/plugin.ts:452), never exported. The one real shipped MountCapability (apigen-plugin-health) hand-builds the full ~10-field Operation literal itself, including a locally-reimplemented seg() helper to avoid a cross-package dependency. Required change: extract and ship a REAL syntheticOp(id, descriptor, fields) helper in apigen-core-client as part of this work, and retrofit apigen-plugin-health onto it in the same change so there is exactly one implementation, not two independently-maintained ones.

F3 — No cross-host contract; invokeBatch/MountCapability is TS-only today with nothing to port. PluginLanguage already includes py/rust/go/java, and a Python runtime already exists (packages/apigen/python/apigen_python/runtime.py, its own invoke/invoke_sync) entirely separate from the TS createInvoker/Layer/MountCapability types. MountedOperation.handler's signature is a TS closure type, not expressible in the Python runtime's model at all. Required change: specify BatchOptions/BatchItemResult as a wire-level JSON-Schema IR independent of the TS invokeBatch function signature (the same separation apigen already uses for Operation's type IR generally) so each host runtime implements fan-out against that wire contract, none depending on the TS implementation.

F4 — BatchOptions is missing per-item cancellation/timeout, will force a breaking change. Call.signal is whole-request cancellation already wired per single op; invokeBatch fans out N invoke() calls but never states whether an individual item's failure/timeout can be cancelled independently of the batch, or whether whole-batch abort propagates to in-flight items. Given onItemError:'continue' is the stated default, 'bound one slow item without killing the whole batch' is near-certain to be requested immediately after ship (it's close to the exact motivating scenario - agent-mcp dispatching to a slow external service per call). Required change: state explicitly whether each fanned-out item gets its own signal derived/linked from the batch's signal, and add itemTimeoutMs?: number to BatchOptions now (even as a stub) so the shape doesn't need a breaking revision on first request.

F5 — Two consumption paths (--use loader vs. hand-wired capabilities.mount.operations()) need an explicit equivalence guarantee. Both paths are legitimate but only acceptable if guaranteed to produce IDENTICAL MountedOperation[] output for the same (descriptor, opts) - otherwise a hand-wiring consumer (like backlog) silently forks from CLI behavior as the plugin evolves. Nothing in the current proposal states or tests this. Required change: state it as an explicit invariant and add a conformance test (analogous to apigen-engine-conformance's existing role) that drives both paths against a fixture descriptor and diffs the output.

F6 (non-blocking, just record it) — Tenet 1 compliance (never derive behavior from source annotations) is already satisfied by the exclude opt-out and dynamic per-item validation reuse; worth stating explicitly in the eventual design doc so a future reviewer doesn't re-litigate it.

Reviewer's summary: ship this, but close F1-F4 before the shape hardens into public API. F1 and F3 are the two most consequential for surviving contact with a second host language and a second transport family; F2 and F5 are cheap to fix now and expensive to retrofit later.

apigen-plugin-cli-output cannot render an operation whose top-level input schema is a discriminated union (oneOf at the schema root) - generates zero flags

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, while designing generic bulk/batch operation support for apigen (FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001) and checking whether apigen's own established discriminated-union convention (`oneOf` + `discriminator`, per `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts`, DESIGN §4.1 `docs/plan/apigen-logical-types`) can be used as an OPERATION's top-level input shape.

**Root cause (traced to real code, not guessed):** `apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts`'s per-operation flag emission (lines ~110-155) calls `dataSchemaProps(fnSchema)`/`dataParamNames(fnSchema)`, both of which read `fnSchema.input.properties` directly and iterate that flat map to emit one `--flag` per property. `schema-introspect.ts`'s existing `oneOf` handling (`FlagProp.oneOf`, per `BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ONEOF-001`) is narrowly scoped to detecting a NESTED optional field's nullable-union shape (`T | undefined` → `oneOf: [{type:'null'},{type:X}]` as `ts-json-schema-generator` renders it) - it is not, and was never meant to be, a mechanism for a top-level discriminated union covering the WHOLE operation input.

**Impact:** if any operation's top-level `input` schema is `{oneOf: [...], discriminator: {...}}` (apigen's own canonical shape for a tagged/variant value, already used elsewhere in the system for field-level unions) rather than a flat `{type:'object', properties:{...}}`, `dataSchemaProps`/`dataParamNames` find no top-level `properties` to iterate at all. The generated CLI command for that operation would have ZERO flags - not degraded, genuinely unusable via CLI. This affects ANY future operation whose input is inherently a top-level union, not just batch (batch is simply the first concrete case that surfaced it).

**Fix direction:** teach `apigen-plugin-cli-output`'s codegen to recognize a root-level `oneOf`+`discriminator` operation input and render it as N Commander subcommands, one per discriminator branch (e.g. a hypothetical `batch` operation would render as `<cli> batch create-item --items ...` / `<cli> batch task --items ...`), with each branch's own flat `properties` rendered via the EXISTING flag-generation logic unchanged (once inside one branch, it's a flat object again - no new logic needed there). MCP (`apigen-plugin-mcp`) and HTTP/runtime validation are unaffected by this gap - MCP passes the raw JSON schema through to the client/LLM as `inputSchema` with no per-property decomposition, and the existing validate-layer already evaluates `oneOf` correctly at dispatch time.

**Explicitly non-blocking:** this does NOT gate or need to be resolved as a prerequisite for any consumer of the `oneOf`+`discriminator` convention (e.g. FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001's batch operation) to ship for MCP/HTTP first - CLI catches up independently on its own timeline, the same pattern this repo already uses for `apigen-plugin-cli-output`'s existing streaming-rejection gap (`FEAT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-008`/`DEBT-APIGEN-SERVE-CORE-002`'s cli half) not blocking HTTP/MCP streaming support.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, apigen-batch-design-2026-07-25, 1: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/generate.ts:110-155 (dataSchemaProps/dataParamNames property-iteration, no oneOf-root handling); 2: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-cli-output/src/lib/schema-introspect.ts:29-54 (FlagProp.oneOf scoped to nested nullable-field detection only, BUG-APIGEN-CLI-ONEOF-001); 3: packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts (apigen's own canonical oneOf+discriminator convention for tagged unions); 4: packages/apigen/apigen-plugin-mcp/src/lib/generate.ts (contrast - no per-property decomposition, unaffected)]

content:
apigen has no JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration codegen path for any operation - a real gap in the core value proposition, not just a batch-spec detail

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, during an architect revision pass on `docs/spec/apigen/BATCH_0.0.1.md` (FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001), while resolving whether `oneOf`+`discriminator` schemas degrade to a looser type when consumed by this repo's JSON-Schema→TS codegen.

**Finding:** the premise didn't hold - **there is no JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration codegen path anywhere in this repo**, for `_batch` or any other operation (verified via `grep -rn "json-schema-to-typescript|jsonSchemaToTs|generateTypes" packages/apigen`, zero hits outside node_modules/dist). `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/ts-json-schema.ts` runs the OPPOSITE direction (TS source → JSON Schema, via `ts-json-schema-generator`+`ts-morph`) and has zero references to `oneOf`/`discriminator`/`union`.

What DOES exist, all real and already correctly handling `oneOf`+`discriminator`: the JSON-Schema wire shape itself (`union.ts` nominal/$ref, `morph-walk.ts` inline/advisory), OpenAPI emission (`packages/apigen/codegen/openapi`, which just passes oneOf/discriminator through since OpenAPI 3.1 natively supports it), runtime encode/decode transcoding (`apigen-base-logical/src/lib/emit.ts`'s `emitOneOf`), runtime validation (`apigen-engine-runtime/src/lib/validate-layer.ts`, which deliberately does NOT use Ajv's built-in `discriminator:true` for compatibility reasons), and runtime dispatch (`union-codec.ts` routing by `discriminator.propertyName`/`.mapping`).

**Why this matters beyond batch:** apigen's stated purpose (per `docs/apigen/SPEC.md` Tenet 0) is code-first extraction that projects to every transport/target including "clients." Today, a consumer gets typed access only by being in the SAME monorepo and importing the hand-authored source functions directly (or via `codegen/openapi`'s output being fed to an EXTERNAL, non-apigen-built codegen tool). There is no first-party "generate a typed TS client SDK from the descriptor" output - a real, load-bearing gap for any cross-service or cross-language consumer that isn't just importing the same TS source file.

**Not urgent/blocking for FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001** - the architect's finding was specifically that this absence introduces NO additional risk to the batch design (nothing about `_batch`'s `oneOf`+`discriminator` shape would behave differently here than any other operation with a union-shaped field already does). But the gap itself is real and worth its own tracked item, independent of batch.

**Fix direction:** scope a JSON-Schema→TS-type-declaration generator (or adopt/wrap an existing one, e.g. `json-schema-to-typescript`) as a new apigen codegen target (`--type ts-client` or similar), with `_batch`'s discriminated-union branches used as one of its first fixtures once it exists (so this exact case is proven, not assumed).

**Status:** OPEN.

content:
union.ts (nominal/$ref) vs morph-walk.ts (inline/advisory) are two distinct discriminated-union mechanisms with no doc distinguishing them - easy to pick the wrong one, and both share an undocumented ≥2-variant constraint

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, during design work on `FEAT-APIGEN-BULK-OPS-001` (generic batch operations) - the design's own author (a Claude session) initially cited `apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts` as the mechanism for `_batch`'s discriminated-union input schema. An architect revision pass caught that this was the WRONG one: `union.ts`'s `buildUnionSchema` (verified `union.ts:111-139`) only emits `$ref`-based branches into `#/$defs/<ClassName>`, requires each variant to be a *nominal* type already registered by `nominal.ts`, and throws (`union.ts:114-118`) below 2 variants. The actual fit for synthetically-constructed, non-nominal inline branches is `morph-walk.ts`'s `InlineDiscriminator`/`detectDiscriminator` (`morph-walk.ts:276-287,298-309`), whose own doc comment explicitly contrasts itself with `union.ts` ("unlike `union.ts`'s `$ref`-based `buildUnionSchema`, the mapping target is a same-document pointer") - meaning the codebase already documents the distinction, just not anywhere a plugin author would find it before picking one.

**Compounding issue:** BOTH builders independently enforce the same undocumented invariant - a discriminated union needs ≥2 variants (`union.ts:114-118` throws; `morph-walk.ts`'s `detectDiscriminator` returns `undefined` below 2, `morph-walk.ts:301`). Any future `MountCapability`/plugin author building a schema whose variant count is descriptor-dependent (unknown until runtime, as with batch's "one branch per batchable operation") needs to know this and explicitly handle the 0-or-1-variant case (e.g. don't mount at all) - today this is discoverable only by reading both files' internals or by hitting the thrown error/silent `undefined` in practice.

**Fix direction:** add a short comparison note (a doc comment on `MountCapability` in `plugin.ts`, and/or a README section in `schema-builders/`) stating: (1) `union.ts` is for nominal, already-extracted TS classes needing `$ref`+`$defs` identity; `morph-walk.ts`'s inline discriminator is for synthetically-constructed, non-nominal branches (e.g. a dynamically-sized mount-contributed union); (2) both require ≥2 variants - a caller constructing a union whose size depends on runtime/descriptor state MUST handle the <2-variant case explicitly (e.g. contribute zero synthetic operations) rather than assume a union is always constructible.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, architect-reviewer, apigen-batch-spec-revision, docs/spec/apigen/BATCH_0.0.1.md §1.1 (round-2 correction); packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/union.ts:111-139; packages/apigen/apigen-core-client/src/lib/schema-builders/morph-walk.ts:276-287,283-284,298-309]

backlog_append_note/backlog_get_item fail with an unhelpful "item not found" when humanId is correct but repo string doesn't exactly match how the item was filed - no hint that the item exists under a different repo value

**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, writing 25 real triage-verdict notes back onto agent-mcp-related backlog items after a triage sweep. 5 of 25 `backlog_append_note` calls failed with `MCP error -32603: backlog item not found: PseudoSky/adhd::agent-mcp-00X` even though every other sibling item in the same batch (same apparent project, same naming convention) succeeded under `repo:"PseudoSky/adhd"`.

**Root cause:** those 5 items (`agent-mcp-001`, `agent-mcp-002`, `agent-mcp-004`, `agent-mcp-005`, `agent-mcp-006`) were filed at some earlier point with `repo:"adhd"` (bare, no `PseudoSky/` prefix) instead of the `"PseudoSky/adhd"` convention every other item in the same logical project uses. Confirmed via `backlog_list_items` grep: `humanId:"agent-mcp-002"` exists exactly once, with `repo:"adhd"` on file - `backlog_get_item({repo:"PseudoSky/adhd", humanId:"agent-mcp-002"})` doesn't error, it silently returns a null result (itself a separate, likely-related bug - see `BUG-APIGEN-LOGICAL-NULL-OBJECT-RESULT-INT64-001`, the returned shape was literally `{"$apigen":"int64","v":"null"}`, that bug's own broken null-encoding leaking through here), while `backlog_append_note` with the same wrong repo throws the less-ambiguous but still unhelpful `-32603 item not found`.

**Impact (UX/DX):** the error message gives zero signal that the item exists under a different `repo` value - it reads identically to "this humanId was never filed at all." A caller (human or agent) has no way to distinguish "typo'd the humanId" from "right humanId, wrong repo key" without manually grep-searching the whole backlog for the humanId string and comparing repo fields by hand, which is what this session had to do. Compounded by the fact that `repo` inconsistency ('adhd' vs 'PseudoSky/adhd' vs presumably others) is apparently already possible to create in this backlog store today with no validation catching it at write time.

**Fix direction (two independent, complementary changes):**
1. **Better error, not a silent/ambiguous failure:** when a `(repo, humanId)` lookup misses but the `humanId` exists under a DIFFERENT `repo` value, the error/response should say so explicitly (e.g. `"item 'agent-mcp-002' not found for repo 'PseudoSky/adhd' - did you mean repo 'adhd'?"`), rather than a bare not-found. This alone would have saved several minutes of manual cross-referencing this session.
2. **Prevent the drift at write time:** `backlog_create_item` (and `importFromMarkdown`) should validate/normalize `repo` against a canonical known-repo list (or at minimum warn) rather than silently accepting an arbitrary string that happens to look plausible - this is presumably how the 5 items ended up on the wrong value in the first place.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: live repro this session - 5 of 25 backlog_append_note calls against humanIds agent-mcp-001/002/004/005/006 with repo:"PseudoSky/adhd" failed with "item not found", succeeded identically once repo:"adhd" was substituted; 2: backlog_get_item({repo:"PseudoSky/adhd", humanId:"agent-mcp-002"}) returned {"$apigen":"int64","v":"null"} rather than an error, cross-referencing BUG-APIGEN-LOGICAL-NULL-OBJECT-RESULT-INT64-001's known null-encoding defect]

Three concrete, currently-live mechanisms replace the described gap: (1) entrypoint/backlog/src/store/query.ts:117-125 `findItemNode` now throws `AmbiguousHumanIdError` on >1 live match instead of silently picking one — this directly kills the 'TASK-001 dual-repo silent wrong item' danger class described in my routing instructions. (2) entrypoint/backlog/src/store/query.ts:163-174 `buildNotFoundError`/`findHumanIdInAnyRepo` — a repo/humanId lookup miss now throws `BacklogItemNotFoundError` carrying `foundInRepos: string[]` naming the actual repo(s) the id lives under, instead of a bare null (wired into `getItem`, entrypoint/backlog/src/client.ts:111-116). (3) entrypoint/backlog/src/store/query.ts:145-159 `knownRepos()` backs a proactive discovery/warning surface: `createItemNode` (entrypoint/backlog/src/store/crud.ts:289-290) and `importFromMarkdown` (entrypoint/backlog/src/client.ts:313-317) both emit a `repoWarning` listing every existing repo value in the store when a caller uses a repo string the store hasn't seen before ('existing repo value(s) here: ...'). Separately, the blanket premise 'requires passing repo as a filter everywhere' is also false as stated: `BacklogFilter.repo` (entrypoint/backlog/src/model.ts:320) and `StatsScope.repo` (model.ts:377, doc: 'absent + global scope ⇒ cross-repo rollup') are both optional — `listItems`/`stats`/`spotlight`/`readyItems`/`dependencyGraph`/`topoOrder` all default to a global cross-repo view. `stats()` called with no scope additionally returns `byRepo: Record<string,number>` (query.ts:199, `scope.repo === undefined ? countByKey(...) : {}`) — a live, general-purpose 'which repos exist and how many items each has' tool, already exposed as an MCP tool via client.ts:136 `stats`. Repo IS still required only for single-item mutations (getItem/updateItem/claim*/transitionStatus etc.) which is architecturally correct since humanId is only unique within a repo, not a UX gap. meta_parsed.title: backlog_append_note/backlog_get_item fail with an unhelpful "item not found" when humanId is correct but repo string doesn't exactly match how the item was filed - no hint that the item exists under a different repo value
meta_parsed.body:
**Discovered:** 2026-07-25, writing 25 real triage-verdict notes back onto agent-mcp-related backlog items after a triage sweep. 5 of 25 `backlog_append_note` calls failed with `MCP error -32603: backlog item not found: PseudoSky/adhd::agent-mcp-00X` even though every other sibling item in the same batch (same apparent project, same naming convention) succeeded under `repo:"PseudoSky/adhd"`.

**Root cause:** those 5 items (`agent-mcp-001`, `agent-mcp-002`, `agent-mcp-004`, `agent-mcp-005`, `agent-mcp-006`) were filed at some earlier point with `repo:"adhd"` (bare, no `PseudoSky/` prefix) instead of the `"PseudoSky/adhd"` convention every other item in the same logical project uses. Confirmed via `backlog_list_items` grep: `humanId:"agent-mcp-002"` exists exactly once, with `repo:"adhd"` on file - `backlog_get_item({repo:"PseudoSky/adhd", humanId:"agent-mcp-002"})` doesn't error, it silently returns a null result (itself a separate, likely-related bug - see `BUG-APIGEN-LOGICAL-NULL-OBJECT-RESULT-INT64-001`, the returned shape was literally `{"$apigen":"int64","v":"null"}`, that bug's own broken null-encoding leaking through here), while `backlog_append_note` with the same wrong repo throws the less-ambiguous but still unhelpful `-32603 item not found`.

**Impact (UX/DX):** the error message gives zero signal that the item exists under a different `repo` value - it reads identically to "this humanId was never filed at all." A caller (human or agent) has no way to distinguish "typo'd the humanId" from "right humanId, wrong repo key" without manually grep-searching the whole backlog for the humanId string and comparing repo fields by hand, which is what this session had to do. Compounded by the fact that `repo` inconsistency ('adhd' vs 'PseudoSky/adhd' vs presumably others) is apparently already possible to create in this backlog store today with no validation catching it at write time.

**Fix direction (two independent, complementary changes):**
1. **Better error, not a silent/ambiguous failure:** when a `(repo, humanId)` lookup misses but the `humanId` exists under a DIFFERENT `repo` value, the error/response should say so explicitly (e.g. `"item 'agent-mcp-002' not found for repo 'PseudoSky/adhd' - did you mean repo 'adhd'?"`), rather than a bare not-found. This alone would have saved several minutes of manual cross-referencing this session.
2. **Prevent the drift at write time:** `backlog_create_item` (and `importFromMarkdown`) should validate/normalize `repo` against a canonical known-repo list (or at minimum warn) rather than silently accepting an arbitrary string that happens to look plausible - this is presumably how the 5 items ended up on the wrong value in the first place.

**Status:** OPEN.
Citations: [main, claude, agent-mcp-backlog-triage-2026-07-25, 1: live repro this session - 5 of 25 backlog_append_note calls against humanIds agent-mcp-001/002/004/005/006 with repo:"PseudoSky/adhd" failed with "item not found", succeeded identically once repo:"adhd" was substituted; 2: backlog_get_item({repo:"PseudoSky/adhd", humanId:"agent-mcp-002"}) returned {"$apigen":"int64","v":"null"} rather than an error, cross-referencing BUG-APIGEN-LOGICAL-NULL-OBJECT-RESULT-INT64-001's known null-encoding defect]

notes.text: Fixed both halves, live-verified against the real repro data (agent-mcp-002 filed under repo=adhd): get-item and append-note called with repo=PseudoSky/adhd now throw BacklogItemNotFoundError(...did you mean repo 'adhd'?) instead of silent-null/bare-not-found. createItem/importFromMarkdown now emit a soft repoWarning (never blocks the write) when repo is new to the store. Added 14 new real-store tests (repo-lookup-ux.spec.ts); nx test backlog 117/117 green, nx lint backlog clean, nx build backlog green.

ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET not configured — all anthropic-provider agents fail at task time

ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-25 (debugger session). Original body incorrectly stated "the config file / .local.yaml layer is the intended mechanism" — this is FALSE, proven by code below. Filed BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001 (cross-linked) for the code-level defect (misleading remediation message + missing secret-ref wiring); this DEBT item is retained for the missing-user-config aspect / doc fix.

Proven mechanism (not inference):
1. Provider secrets (ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET etc.) are declared in PROVIDER_DEFAULTS, entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/config.ts:210-213 — but deliberately NOT declared as FieldSpecs in agentMcpEnvironmentSpec.config (config.ts:63-189; module doc comment config.ts:11-19 explicitly notes this).
2. getProviderConfig() (config.ts:233-256) resolves the secret via env.resolveEnvName(defaults.secret) (config.ts:248); the startup check verifyAgentEnvRefs() (entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/index.ts:169-198) does the same at index.ts:188.
3. Environment.resolveEnvName() (packages/environment/environment-core-node/src/environment.ts:317-320): `if (!this.isEnvNameAllowed(name)) return undefined; return process.env[name];` — reads ONLY live process.env, zero file-layer fallback.
4. The file-layer cascade (system→global→project→local config.yaml/config.local.yaml) is resolveConfig() in packages/environment/environment-builder/src/config-resolver.ts:143-193, iterating Object.keys(configSpec) (line 154) — ONLY declared FieldSpec keys get file-layer treatment. resolveConfig runs exactly once, inside the Environment constructor (environment.ts:228); resolveEnvName never calls it and has no path to the layered config at all.
5. So a value placed in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml for ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET is silently inert — never read. Only a literal env var already present in process.env (shell export, or an MCP host's .mcp.json per-server env:{} block) works.
6. verifyAgentEnvRefs()'s own warning text (index.ts:194-196) says 'Set them in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml or the environment directly' — the config.local.yaml half is provably false per (3)-(5) and will never fix the warning.
7. Regression vs. pre-redesign: commit 9681e0c8 (2026-06-27, 'centralize env via config.ts, unify provider credentials') shipped packages/ai/agent-mcp/src/utils/load-env.ts — loadEnvHierarchy() loaded <cwd>/.env > <cwd>/.adhd/.env > ~/.adhd/.env into process.env via dotenv BEFORE any config read, so a secret kept in ~/.adhd/.env (the historical location) worked. The @adhd/environment zero-config redesign (ARCHITECTURE.md) removed this loader with no replacement for secret-shaped values — confirmed via zero dotenv hits under entrypoint/agent-mcp/src, and the shipped marketing copy at entrypoint/agent-mcp/docs/marketing/.catalog/capabilities.json:513 ('No dotenv .env files ... the pre-redesign .adhd/.env / .env / load-env.js cascade was removed'). The redesign's own FieldSpec.secret:true mechanism (ARCHITECTURE.md §3.1 line 85: 'stored as env-ref, resolved at runtime'; implemented at config-resolver.ts:157,184-188) was purpose-built to give exactly this kind of value file-layer + env-ref treatment — but config.ts:386's own comment concedes the spec 'declares none' (no field is marked secret:true). The intended replacement mechanism exists in the package but was never wired up for provider credentials.

User-facing fix (works today, no code change): export ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET (etc.) as a real process env var — in the parent shell before launching agent-mcp, or under the relevant .mcp.json server entry's env:{} block (see .mcp.json's agent-mcp-published entry for the existing pattern). config.local.yaml does NOT work for this and must not be recommended until BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001 lands.

Discovered: 2026-07-25 during agent-mcp debug session (original filing); root-caused same day.
