meta_parsed.title: ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET not configured — all anthropic-provider agents fail at task time
meta_parsed.body:
ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-25 (debugger session). Original body incorrectly stated "the config file / .local.yaml layer is the intended mechanism" — this is FALSE, proven by code below. Filed BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001 (cross-linked) for the code-level defect (misleading remediation message + missing secret-ref wiring); this DEBT item is retained for the missing-user-config aspect / doc fix.

Proven mechanism (not inference):
1. Provider secrets (ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET etc.) are declared in PROVIDER_DEFAULTS, entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/config.ts:210-213 — but deliberately NOT declared as FieldSpecs in agentMcpEnvironmentSpec.config (config.ts:63-189; module doc comment config.ts:11-19 explicitly notes this).
2. getProviderConfig() (config.ts:233-256) resolves the secret via env.resolveEnvName(defaults.secret) (config.ts:248); the startup check verifyAgentEnvRefs() (entrypoint/agent-mcp/src/index.ts:169-198) does the same at index.ts:188.
3. Environment.resolveEnvName() (packages/environment/environment-core-node/src/environment.ts:317-320): `if (!this.isEnvNameAllowed(name)) return undefined; return process.env[name];` — reads ONLY live process.env, zero file-layer fallback.
4. The file-layer cascade (system→global→project→local config.yaml/config.local.yaml) is resolveConfig() in packages/environment/environment-builder/src/config-resolver.ts:143-193, iterating Object.keys(configSpec) (line 154) — ONLY declared FieldSpec keys get file-layer treatment. resolveConfig runs exactly once, inside the Environment constructor (environment.ts:228); resolveEnvName never calls it and has no path to the layered config at all.
5. So a value placed in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml for ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET is silently inert — never read. Only a literal env var already present in process.env (shell export, or an MCP host's .mcp.json per-server env:{} block) works.
6. verifyAgentEnvRefs()'s own warning text (index.ts:194-196) says 'Set them in ~/.adhd/agent-mcp/production/config.local.yaml or the environment directly' — the config.local.yaml half is provably false per (3)-(5) and will never fix the warning.
7. Regression vs. pre-redesign: commit 9681e0c8 (2026-06-27, 'centralize env via config.ts, unify provider credentials') shipped packages/ai/agent-mcp/src/utils/load-env.ts — loadEnvHierarchy() loaded <cwd>/.env > <cwd>/.adhd/.env > ~/.adhd/.env into process.env via dotenv BEFORE any config read, so a secret kept in ~/.adhd/.env (the historical location) worked. The @adhd/environment zero-config redesign (ARCHITECTURE.md) removed this loader with no replacement for secret-shaped values — confirmed via zero dotenv hits under entrypoint/agent-mcp/src, and the shipped marketing copy at entrypoint/agent-mcp/docs/marketing/.catalog/capabilities.json:513 ('No dotenv .env files ... the pre-redesign .adhd/.env / .env / load-env.js cascade was removed'). The redesign's own FieldSpec.secret:true mechanism (ARCHITECTURE.md §3.1 line 85: 'stored as env-ref, resolved at runtime'; implemented at config-resolver.ts:157,184-188) was purpose-built to give exactly this kind of value file-layer + env-ref treatment — but config.ts:386's own comment concedes the spec 'declares none' (no field is marked secret:true). The intended replacement mechanism exists in the package but was never wired up for provider credentials.

User-facing fix (works today, no code change): export ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET (etc.) as a real process env var — in the parent shell before launching agent-mcp, or under the relevant .mcp.json server entry's env:{} block (see .mcp.json's agent-mcp-published entry for the existing pattern). config.local.yaml does NOT work for this and must not be recommended until BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001 lands.

Discovered: 2026-07-25 during agent-mcp debug session (original filing); root-caused same day.

loadEnvHierarchy loads ~/.adhd/.env, <cwd>/.adhd/.env, <cwd>/.env into process.env — RESTORED for BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001: the @adhd/environment redesign left no file-population mechanism
agent-mcp env block forwards only ADHD_ENV_SCOPE/ADHD_AGENT_CONFIG/ADHD_AGENT_REGISTRY_DB_PATH — no ADHD_AGENT_ANTHROPIC_SECRET (shell env var UNSET in this session)

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-12 for EPIC-DISPATCH-02: repo-root .mcp.json's agent-mcp server env block still carries only ADHD_ENV_SCOPE/ADHD_AGENT_CONFIG/ADHD_AGENT_REGISTRY_DB_PATH -- zero ADHD_AGENT_<PROVIDER>_SECRET forwarding, and the agent-mcp-published entry has no env block at all. Still blocks EPIC-DISPATCH-02 AC3 (anthropic-provider task completing under THIS repo's MCP wiring) unless the operator's shell already exports the secret (relies on ~/.adhd/.env via load-env.ts, not on this repo's .mcp.json). Priority should be CRITICAL, not MEDIUM, for this epic -- it is a hard precondition, not a nice-to-have.

notes.text: Revalidated 2026-08-02: PARTIAL/mitigated — shell env UNSET and .mcp.json does not forward it, BUT ~/.adhd/.env:4 configures it and loadEnvHierarchy() restores process.env at server start (restored for BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001, regression-tested). Standard launch path resolves; stripped-env launch still fails.

Proposed spec from the 2026-08-08 architect planning pass. This item's premise was NOT verified against current code by that pass — confirm the premise still holds before implementing any of this. Also referenced in the artifact's collision analysis as P23.

Agent: devops-engineer. Files: `entrypoint/agent-mcp/README.md`, `live-budget.e2e.test.ts`, `live-dag.e2e.test.ts`, `live-oauth.e2e.test.ts`, `utils/load-env.ts`, `.mcp.json`.

Context per artifact: `load-env.ts`'s runtime fix is already shipped (its header allegedly cites 'RESTORED for BUG-MCP-CREDENTIALS-001') — remaining work is documentation only.

Acceptance: README names an owner for the `AGENT_MCP_LIVE`/`AGENT_MCP_BUDGET_LIVE` gate per AGENTS.md §7; documents the real credential-source cascade (process.env / ~/.adhd/.env / <cwd>/.adhd/.env / <cwd>/.env), explicitly stating that config.local.yaml does NOT populate secrets.

Verification: Grep the updated README for the required owner name and the corrected credential-source statement; cross-reference from all 3 e2e test file headers.

Dependency framing: `.mcp.json` collision (MCP host config = W2-10/P17, Wave 2; this packet = P23, Wave 3; gitnexus mandate = W4-4/P31, Wave 4) — sequenced across 3 waves, file-lock only per §1b.

Risk note: Proposed spec, premise not verified. No specific Risk Register entry.

RESCOPED 2026-08-12 (re-verification of poisoned-run judgement, live evidence). Reverting the false escalation: this item's own 2026-08-02 note already correctly recorded the mitigated truth ('~/.adhd/.env:4 configures it and loadEnvHierarchy() restores process.env at server start ... Standard launch path resolves'), consistent with the Live Credential Truth -- config.ts:37 unconditionally calls loadEnvHierarchy() before any secret lookup, populating process.env from ~/.adhd/.env regardless of what .mcp.json forwards. The title and the 2026-08-12 EPIC-DISPATCH-02 citation note ('unless the operator's shell already exports the secret ... Priority should be CRITICAL') overclaim/mis-describe the mechanism -- it is NOT shell-export-dependent, it's an unconditional file read (~/.adhd/.env) on every server start, independent of .mcp.json and independent of the launching shell's own env.

Corrected scope: narrow to '.mcp.json does not EXPLICITLY forward ADHD_AGENT_<PROVIDER>_SECRET (relies implicitly on the ~/.adhd/.env fallback via loadEnvHierarchy, which works for the standard launch path but would fail if ~/.adhd/.env is absent or lacks a given provider's secret -- e.g. CI, a different user, a stripped-env launch)'. A real defense-in-depth/explicitness gap, not a hard blocker to standard task-calling. Priority reverted from the false CRITICAL escalation back to MEDIUM.
